tob-10497: The Jewish historian Josephus wrote this massive history in the first century AD, retelling the whole story of the Jewish people from Adam to his own time. Drawing on the Bible and lost sources, he gives the outside world’s clearest window onto ancient Judaism. His account of the Roman destruction of Jerusalem remains the main source for those fateful events.
tob-10797: Anthropologist Frederick Starr’s illustrated survey introduces Korean Buddhism — its temples, its thousand-year history, and its distinctive art. He describes how the faith traveled from China and took root in Korean soil, producing its own monastic traditions and masterpieces of sculpture. The book remains a rare early English window onto Korea’s Buddhist heritage.
cia-0000107297: From June 1991, a report on officials offering what they called concrete proof of an American pilot's death. For families of the missing, such proof — a crash site, remains, records — was the only thing that could end decades of not knowing. The misspelled title in the archive cannot hide the human weight of the subject.
cia-0000107497: Carrying an estimated publication date of September 1963, this study examines communist-bloc economic activity in Cuba from 1960 through mid-1963. Soviet aid, trade deals, and technicians were turning Cuba into Moscow's outpost in the Americas. The report measures, in dollars and tons, how deeply the island had been pulled into the Soviet orbit.
cia-0000109797: A July 1981 weekly terrorism report carrying an article about Clifford Bevens — the truncated title hides the details. Weeklies like this one mixed incident summaries with deeper pieces on people and groups. The entry is a reminder that behind every terrorism statistic in these files, there were individual stories.
cia-0000119697: An August 1951 estimate of probable world developments through mid-1953. The Korean War was raging, Stalin was alive, and the future looked dark. The document is the intelligence community's best guess at where the world was heading — written when the Cold War was at its coldest.
cia-0000132097: An April 1961 clandestine services history — the truncated title withholds the operation. Internal histories were the CIA's institutional memory, written for insiders. The entry guards its subject behind a clipped title, but promises the agency's own account of secret work.
cia-0000132497: A January 1961 report that Colombia might break relations with Cuba. Bogota was weighing the diplomatic divorce. The document is the hemisphere's cold shoulder: one more capital, ready to walk away.
cia-0000135997: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN on the use of lawyers at the conference. Even covert action needed counsel. The document is the counsel: the lawyers, deployed.
cia-0000136097: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for LUGTON with training concerns for Calligeris. The exile chief's preparation, worried over. The document is the concern: the training, questioned.
cia-0000136197: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for RAZMARA on starting Operation A and an underground bulletin. The covert press, launched. The document is the start: the operation, begun — the bulletin, printed.
cia-0000136297: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN with a command message for CADICK on revising unconventional tactics — the truncated title cuts off the details. The playbook, updated. The document is the revision: the tactics, rethought.
cia-0000136397: A 1954 cable to LINCOLN for CADICK on rifle fabrication. The guns, made. The document is the workshop: the rifles, fabricated.
cia-0000136897: A 1954 cable to the senior representative at LINCOLN requesting answers to questions on PBSUCCESS operations — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The quiz, administered upward. The document is the questions: the answers, demanded.
cia-0000136997: A 1954 cable on a reference to KUBARK in the press. The agency's cryptonym surfaced publicly — a security scare. The document is the leak: the name, printed.
cia-0000140397: A 1952 document — subject deleted — an interview about ARTICHOKE, the mind-control program. The program, discussed. The entry is the interview: the subject, hidden — the topic, infamous.
un-ga-res-997: UN General Assembly Resolution 997, adopted in November 1956 — the emergency session's demand for an immediate ceasefire in the Suez Crisis. As the invasion of Egypt unfolded, the Assembly ordered the guns to stop. Paired with Resolution 998, it was the world's answer to aggression. The resolution is the order: the ceasefire, demanded.
un-sc-res-397: Security Council Resolution 397, cataloged with the year 1974 — the numbering suggests 1976, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
un-sc-res-997: Security Council Resolution 997, cataloged with the year 1993 — the numbering suggests 1995, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
un-sc-res-1297: Security Council Resolution 1297, adopted in May 2000 — the Ethiopia-Eritrea resolution, demanding an immediate end to the fighting between the two Horn of Africa neighbors. The Council tried to stop one of Africa's deadliest border wars. The resolution is the demand: the war, halted — on paper.
cia-0000135897: A 1954 CIA file — general political action, deleted conversations; specific debriefing, the truncated title suggests. The Guatemala coup year's tradecraft. The document is the action: the conversations, deleted — the debriefing, specific.
cia-0000136697: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000136697. The fateful year's firm-dated papers. The document is the firmness: the year, certain.
un-sc-res-97: Security Council Resolution 97, adopted in 1952 — aligned. The early-fifties Council deliberated. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d97: Marshal Stalin to President Roosevelt, November 5, 1943 — Document 97. Moscow wrote the same day. The message is the parallel: two leaders, one day.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d197: President Roosevelt to Prime Minister Churchill, November 8, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 197. Washington to London. The message is the link: the allies, conferring.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d297: The President to the Secretary of State, November 24, 1943 — Document 297. The White House answered. The message is the answer: the president, to the department.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d397: The Secretary of State to the President, November 30, 1943 — Document 397. The department's month-end briefing. The memo is the month's end: the secretary, informing.
arxiv-2605-08797: Maximum likelihood decoding — finding the most probable message behind a noisy signal — is a classic hard problem, and Rishav Gupta, Bingkai Lin, and Xin Zheng pin down exactly how hard. Assuming the Exponential Time Hypothesis, a standard complexity conjecture, they prove a tight lower bound on approximating the parametrized version. The 2026 paper is theoretical computer science at its most precise.
arxiv-2605-08897: APDS is a rare immune disorder most doctors never see, which makes diagnosis brutally hard. Safa Alsaidi, Tomás Brogueira, Nizar Mahlaoui, and colleagues apply Shapley regression — a method that fairly attributes a prediction to each input factor — to support APDS diagnosis. The 2026 paper is a case study in bringing explainable AI to rare-disease medicine.
arxiv-2605-09197: When humans and AI chatbots mingle, opinions diffuse in new ways — and nobody has measured it well. Léna Gaubert, Rémi Devaux, Elif Çelen, and colleagues propose an experimental method for studying opinion diffusion in human-AI hybrid societies. The 2026 paper is social science for the chatbot age.
arxiv-2605-09797: Navier-Stokes global smoothness is a Millennium Prize problem; the axisymmetric case is more tractable. Rishad Shahmurov offers a classical two-part first-threshold proof via swirl closure and full-system reduction. The 2026 paper is PDE analysis on famous ground.
arxiv-2605-09897: Generative video receivers need error correction that understands meaning, not just bits; tube-structured incremental semantic HARQ delivers it. Xuesong Wang, Xinyan Xie, and Runxin Zhang develop the scheme. The 2026 paper is semantic communications built for next-generation generative video receivers everywhere.
arxiv-2605-09997: LLM graph generation has capability gaps — and they need diagnosing progressively, not all at once. Zihe Wei, Sheng Xiang, Ying Zhang, and Changjun Jiang build GraphInstruct: a progressive benchmark. The 2026 paper is LLM evaluation for graph-shaped thinking. It diagnoses gaps step by step.
arxiv-2605-10097: Scientific literature search, proactively assisted by hierarchical memory — H-MAPS anticipates what you need. Koji Nishikawa and Makoto P. Kato build the assistant. The 2026 paper is scholarly search with foresight. It searches proactively before you even ask.
plos-pone-0003397: Evolutionary biologists probed why some honey bee workers hoard pollen in this 2008 study. The team tested whether the sensory systems driving social behavior are tied to female reproductive traits, using strains bred for heavy versus light pollen storage. Their findings link the bees' social instincts to their reproductive wiring, hinting at a shared genetic toolkit.
plos-pone-0003497: ALS researchers caught a mutant protein misbehaving in this 2008 paper. In familial ALS tied to SOD1 mutations, the team studied misfolded single units of the enzyme sticking to cell surfaces. That adherent misfolded SOD1 may seed the cellular damage behind motor-neuron death, offering a concrete target in the hunt for ALS therapies.
plos-pone-0003597: Cancer biologists Kojic, Wiseman, and Ghaidi eyed a tumor doorway as a drug entrance in this 2008 paper. The motility factor receptor gp78/AMFR, overexpressed in many cancers, pulls its ligand inside through raft-dependent endocytosis. Hijacking that entry route could smuggle therapies straight into tumor cells.
plos-pone-0003697: In 2008, Yerushalmi and Teicher let brain-like plasticity evolve on a computer. Their evolutionary model grew networks whose synapses could change with experience, the basis of learning and memory. Watching plasticity itself evolve offers clues to how real brains came to rewire themselves.
plos-pone-0003797: Kulick, Moccia, and Didelot caught stomach bacteria swapping DNA in patchwork in this 2008 paper. After natural transformation, Helicobacter pylori genomes showed mosaic imports flecked with recipient sequence. The interspersed pattern reveals how this ulcer bug shuffles its genes with neighbors.
plos-pone-0003897: In 2008, Macé, Seyer, and Chemani found the gene cluster behind a germ's slime cities. The bac cluster in Pseudomonas aeruginosa proved involved in biofilm formation. The discovery names the genetic basis of the stubborn films that shield this hospital pathogen.
plos-pone-0003997: In 2008, Kuznetsov and Khokhlatchev found two tumor guards being chopped up. The growth suppressors NORE1A and RASSF1A were cut by calpain enzymes. Calpain-mediated proteolysis offers cancers a new way to silence these brakes. Blocking the chopping could restore the suppressors in tumors that lost them.
plos-pone-0004097: In 2009, Shen, Tesar, and Du showed old immune systems transplant poorly. Aging weakened both inner and outer T cell factors needed for graft success. Recipient T cells from older donors fared worse. The finding urges age-aware transplant care and testing.
plos-pone-0004197: In 2009, Roussel, Carcaud, and Sandoz rethought the busy ant colony. Aversive learning and keen responsiveness reframed social insect behavior. Division of labor looked new through the sharp lens of dislike. The fresh new view enriches the old threshold model greatly.
plos-pone-0004297: In 2009, Murphy, Belmonte, and Shu found plants needing their DNA repairmen. Abasic endonuclease gene homologues proved essential for young Arabidopsis seed growth. The repair genes kept young seeds alive and well. The neat finding links DNA repair to plant fertility.
plos-pone-0358797: Black men with low income and chronic illness face some of the worst health gaps in America. This study asked what a truly fair health intervention would need — in a southern US state, hearing from the men themselves and the people who serve them. The key factors it identifies, from trust to practical access, give program designers a grounded starting point.
plos-pone-0358597: Where should a shop open? This paper uses machine learning to uncover how traditional retailers compete on location, comparing light-asset formats like kiosks with capital-intensive ones like department stores. The analysis shows how the surrounding urban environment tips the balance — practical intelligence for anyone choosing a storefront.
plos-pone-0351697: Training a patient’s own T cells on their tumor, then sending them back in, is immunotherapy at its most personal. This paper published the protocol for a first-in-human phase I/IIa trial of personalised tumour trained lymphocytes in advanced colorectal cancer. The advance-published plan sets the bar for judging safety and early efficacy.
plos-pone-0357497: Drilling glass-fiber composites causes delamination — layers peeling apart around the hole. This paper built a physics-informed neural network framework to predict drilling-induced delamination in GFRP composites. The AI-physics hybrid helps manufacturers choose drill settings that leave clean, strong holes.
plos-pone-0356997: Staphylococcus aureus prefers certain codons over others — and the bias is no accident. This paper studied codon bias variation across the pathogen’s genome. The patterns reveal the evolutionary pressures shaping one of humanity’s most persistent bacterial foes.
plos-pone-0357797: Ketogenic diets change how the liver processes drugs — with real consequences for dosing. This mouse study examined ketogenic diet–induced changes in hepatic drug metabolism, with potential implications for ozanimod pharmacokinetics. The findings warn clinicians that a patient’s diet can quietly alter drug levels.
plos-pone-0356197: China’s hospital resources are distributed with striking unevenness. This study analyzed the efficiency and spatial correlation of health resource allocation across Chinese hospitals. The resulting maps show exactly where medical resources cluster — and the regions left dangerously thin.
plos-pone-0353797: Heat therapy through hot water immersion appeals to men — but does reality match the expectation? This study examined the anticipated uptake and acceptability of heat therapy in males, measuring expectations and perceptions before and after immersion. The before-and-after comparison guides smarter therapy design.
plos-pone-0341397: Training physical education teachers demands curricula centered on student satisfaction and real outcomes. This paper proposed a student satisfaction-oriented framework for evaluating PE teacher education curriculum implementation. The framework gives programs a practical tool for optimizing quality.
plos-pone-0355997: Dopamine D2 blockers that stay out of the brain could protect neurons via prolactin pathways. This multi-stage in silico study identified novel peripherally restricted risperidone-like D2 antagonists for prolactin-mediated neuroprotection. The computational hits are promising leads for a new neuroprotective strategy.
plos-pone-0355197: Physician shortages are pushing hospitals to shift tasks to paramedics — but will the public accept it? This paper studied public social trust and acceptance of task shifting to hospital paramedics. The findings give policymakers a read on the social license for this controversial fix.
plos-pone-0356797: In China’s live commerce boom, service quality drives whether viewers buy again. This paper studied service quality and repurchase intention, with trust as mediator and generational differences as moderator. The model tells streamers and brands exactly what keeps customers coming back.
plos-pone-0356497: Fasciola gigantica — a giant liver fluke — plagues buffaloes across South Asia. This paper proteomically characterized adult flukes recovered from naturally infected buffaloes in Punjab, Pakistan. The protein catalog is a foundation for diagnostics and vaccines against this costly parasite.
plos-pone-0355697: Fission yeasts — humble single-celled fungi — produce spores of surprising morphological diversity. This paper surveyed that diversity across species. The spore catalog enriches our picture of fungal evolution — and gives cell biologists new models for studying the genetics of shape.
plos-pone-0356597: Mandarin tone sandhi — tones changing in context — is usually studied in laboratories, not conversations. This paper studied it in real interaction. The naturalistic findings reveal how tones actually shift when people talk — messier and more interesting than textbook rules suggest.
plos-pone-0354797: Light therapy might heal injured retinas — and fruit flies are the testbed. This paper explored dose-dependent outcomes of photobiomodulation with two infrared wavelengths applied to injured Drosophila retinae. The wavelength and dose findings inch photobiomodulation toward clinical reality for human retinal disease.
plos-pone-0356697: China’s cancer beds aren’t distributed fairly — and the trend matters. This paper tracked equity in oncology bed allocation from 2008 to 2022 with longitudinal data. The fourteen-year equity analysis reveals whether China’s cancer care is converging toward fairness or drifting further apart.
plos-pone-0353997: Pear bruising costs the fruit industry millions — and tissue mechanics predict it. This paper identified pear tissue mechanical parameters by integrating machine learning with optimization methods. The identified parameters let engineers design gentler handling systems that keep pears pristine from orchard to shelf.
plos-pone-0354497: GLP-1 weight-loss drugs can paralyze the stomach — gastroparesis — with frightening consequences. This systematic review synthesized the clinical features, diagnosis, management, and outcomes of GLP-1-induced gastroparesis. The comprehensive review is essential reading as these blockbuster drugs reach millions.
plos-pone-0328697: Universities drown in student feedback — and topic models promise to make sense of it. This paper compared topic modelling techniques for the thematic analysis of student feedback. The head-to-head comparison reveals which algorithms genuinely capture what students are saying — so institutions can act on it rather than merely archive it.
plos-pone-0355397: Children in child protective services custody face higher risks of forced medication and restraint in emergency departments. This paper documented that disparity in a pediatric ED. The findings demand that emergency care confront its differential treatment of society’s most vulnerable children.
plos-pone-0355597: Bridges must be assessed quickly under real traffic — including overloaded trucks. This paper used machine learning for data-driven rapid assessment of bridge responses under mixed traffic with restricted overloaded vehicles. The ML approach gives engineers fast, reliable structural verdicts without closing the bridge.
plos-pone-0355497: Vitreous hemorrhage — bleeding into the eye’s gel — in proliferative diabetic retinopathy may follow seasons. This paper examined seasonal variation in its incidence. The seasonal patterns could help retina clinics anticipate surges — and researchers understand what environmental triggers rupture fragile new vessels.
plos-pone-0355297: Young male tennis players need training that builds both athleticism and tennis-specific skill. This systematic review and meta-analysis examined neuromuscular training’s effects on physical and tennis-specific performance. The pooled evidence gives coaches the training recipes that genuinely elevate young players’ games.
europmc-pmc2820097: Finding depression and schizophrenia in a blood sample is a long-sought goal. This 2010 paper screens blood plasma proteins in patients and controls, hunting for biomarker signatures of both disorders. The authors profile many analytes at once in case-control collections. Their candidate panels suggested blood tests for mental illness might one day be possible.
europmc-pmc2826397: Computer models of biology are only as good as their testing. This 2010 paper describes the DREAM3 challenges, a competition-style effort to rigorously assess systems biology models. The authors lay out the tests and what they revealed. The initiative pushed the field toward honest benchmarking instead of self-reported success.
europmc-pmc2847997: Breast milk may deliver more than nutrition. This 2010 paper identifies microRNA as a new immune-regulatory agent in breast milk. The authors show these tiny RNAs survive digestion and can influence the infant's immune system. The discovery adds a surprising channel of mother-to-child communication.
europmc-pmc2851497: After SARS struck in 2003, a big unknown was how long immune protection lasts. This 2007 paper tracks how long antibody defenses held in SARS survivors. The team charts the fade over years. The timeline data steered hopes for lasting vaccines against related viruses.
europmc-pmc2852297: X-ray beams that map proteins also damage them, warping the maps. This 2010 primer asks what radiation harm is in shape work and why users should mind. The author spells the toll in plain terms. The piece taught crystallographers to spot and curb beam harm.
europmc-pmc2853097: Tiny RNA bits drift in blood, and this 2010 paper hunts them in stomach cancer. The team finds telling microRNAs in plasma of gastric cancer patients. Their haul hints at a blood draw test. The work pushed liquid checks for a stealthy tumor.
europmc-pmc2883597: Tired immune cells in chronic hepatitis C wear many brakes. This 2010 paper shows exhausted HCV-specific CD8 T cells co-express PD-1, 2B4, CD160, and KLRG1, linked to antigen recognition and differentiation. The authors' profile explains the fatigue. Their work informed checkpoint-style therapies.
europmc-pmc2890697: Steroid hormones start as cholesterol, and this 2010 review traces the supply chain. The authors cover how cells take in cholesterol, move it around, and turn it into hormones. Their overview maps a vital pipeline step by step. The review clarifies how cells feed their hormone factories.
europmc-pmc2912897: Hospital safety mood can be gauged, and this 2010 paper tests the gauge. The authors check the AHRQ hospital poll on patient safety culture at many levels. Their testing backs the tool as sound. The work helps hospitals grow safer year by year.
europmc-pmc2923597: Gut germs breach the mucus wall before inflammation erupts in colitis. This 2010 mouse study shows bacteria pierce the inner mucus layer ahead of inflammation in the dextran sulfate colitis model. The authors catch the invasion order. Their finding puts barrier failure at the start of gut disease.
europmc-pmc2984397: Blood chemistry data needs organizing into libraries. This 2010 paper describes sorting mass-spec chemistry data into chemical libraries. The authors' system tames the data flood. Their work aids compound ID. Labs match mystery peaks against the shelves. The library now holds thousands of entries.
europmc-pmc3042897: Bounce-back quizzes needed reviewing. This 2011 paper compares the many scales that claim to measure resilience. The authors rank the tools by quality. Their review guides psychologists. Few scales passed their strict tests. Clinics now pick from the shortlist. The review exposed shaky validation claims.
europmc-pmc3063797: A new virus felled laying ducks. This 2011 paper pins duck egg-drop syndrome on BYD virus, a new flavivirus. The authors identify the culprit. Their work aided poultry health. Egg output crashed across Chinese farms. Vaccines followed once the culprit emerged.
europmc-pmc6520497: Researchers once proposed five data-driven diabetes subgroups to predict who worsens fastest - but do the clusters beat simple clinical measures? This study pitted the subgroup model against straightforward predictors like age and blood sugar. The simpler approach held its own, suggesting fancy clustering adds less value than hoped for forecasting progression and complications.
europmc-pmc6551897: Interleukin-1 is one of the immune system's loudest alarm bells - a cytokine that rallies inflammation against threats but damages tissues when it will not quiet down. This review tours IL-1's role across general pathology: how the IL-1 family grew, where it helps, and where blocking it treats disease. Few immune signals touch as many illnesses.
europmc-pmc6624997: CUT&RUN maps where proteins grip DNA with remarkable sensitivity - but its ultra-low background breaks standard peak-finding. This paper introduces a peak caller built for the method, using sparse enrichment analysis to spot true binding sites amid the quiet. Epigenome mappers get a tool tuned to their data's quirks.
europmc-pmc6689897: KRAS - a notorious cancer gene - was long deemed undruggable: too smooth for drugs to grip. This paper reports the crack in the armor: a hidden pocket on KRAS that small molecules can actually bind. The discovery turned a hopeless target into one of oncology's hottest pursuits.
europmc-pmc6702897: Brains age at different speeds - and a scan can reveal yours. BrainAGE is a neuroimaging biomarker that estimates brain age from MRI; the gap between brain age and birthday measures wear and tear. A decade of studies, reviewed here, shows what the marker has taught us about healthy and diseased aging.
europmc-pmc6717897: A body-wide infection can worsen Alzheimer's - and microglia are the link. This study shows systemic inflammation cripples the brain's cleanup crew: via the NLRP3 inflammasome, microglia lose their ability to clear amyloid-beta. The finding connects peripheral illness to accelerating brain decline.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-597: The UN's books needed disinfecting in 2007 — GAO's report says the world body's oversight could grow teeth with real internal controls in place. The findings press for audit muscle at Turtle Bay. The report's pitch to Congress: keep paying the dues, but start demanding receipts.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-697: The terror-fighting playbook had a missing page in 2007 — GAO's report says U.S. law agencies lacked orders for helping foreign partners hunt terrorists. The findings expose the cooperation gap. The report demands the missing directives: teamwork needs a rulebook.
openalex-w7204882697: Sadness and worry during and after pregnancy affect both mother and baby, yet they often go unnoticed. This review pulled together fifteen studies from 2006 to 2024 to measure how mood disorders in this period shape outcomes. The authors sum up what the research shows about harm to mother and child alike. A careful summary of why a new mother's mental health deserves the same care as her physical healing.
openalex-w7204993797: Modern schooling often treats students as future workers first and people second. This philosophy-of-education article argues that market-style thinking has gone deeper than business methods in schools: it has reshaped what education is for. The author traces the shift from instrumental reason to a market logic that redefines learning's purpose. A challenging critique for readers asking what school is really selling.
openalex-w7204531397: Brazil's prisons hold far more people than they were built for, and the Federal District is no exception. This article studies overcrowding and the shortage of places through the lens of human rights. The authors review norms, court rulings, and international standards. A sobering legal study of what happens when punishment outruns capacity.
openalex-w7204224797: Brazil once reserved schooling for the elite; the republic promised it to all. This article traces the right to education from empire to republic through the country's constitutions. The authors show how each charter redrew who counts as a student. A legal-history study of citizenship learned in the classroom.
pmc-13513997: A 2026 descriptive study of the people enrolled in NeuroGAP-Psychosis, a genetics research program studying psychosis in African populations. The paper lays out the participants' backgrounds and medical details, setting up future work on the genetic roots of conditions like schizophrenia. Because African ancestry is underrepresented in genetic research, this study fills a real gap.
pmc-13456897: This 2026 cross-sectional study of heart patients examines how depression affects quality of life, testing whether fear and related factors mediate the link. Cardiac disease and depression feed each other, and naming the middle steps points to where counseling could help. The work bridges cardiology and mental health.
pmc-13411297: This 2026 multiple sclerosis study found that retinal layer thickness — measured by eye scans — helps stratify risk of progression independent of relapse activity in relapsing-remitting MS. The eye is a window on the brain, and thinning layers flag smoldering disease. The biomarker could reshape monitoring.
pmc-13481097: This 2026 prospective multicenter study reports mid- to long-term outcomes of primary breast augmentation with B-Lite lightweight implants. Lighter implants promise less tissue strain over time, and postmarketing follow-up tests the claim. The data inform implant choice for surgeons and patients.
pmc-13398397: A 2026 paper evaluating a chronic kidney disease e-phenotype — an algorithm that identifies CKD from electronic health record data. Finding kidney disease in records accurately is the foundation of population health management. The study validates the phenotype's identification and characterization.
pmc-13340497: This 2026 study validated the Turkish translation of a nutrition risk screening tool for pediatric cancer. Malnutrition worsens cancer outcomes in children, and validated tools must speak the local language. The validation enables proper screening in Turkish clinics.
pmc-13524097: A 2026 plant biology paper showing that circadian clock transcription factors Reveille 1 and Reveille 8 regulate O-acetylserine cluster genes and sulfur homeostasis. The body clock controls nutrient metabolism in plants too. The regulatory link is the finding.
pmc-13439697: This 2026 mouse genetics paper generated female- or male-biased litters by targeted distortion of sex chromosome transmission. Biasing the sex ratio at the chromosomal level is a striking feat. The technique has applications in agriculture and pest control.
pmc-13530797: This 2026 conference poster found lateral opening wedge distal femoral osteotomy had greater effect on TT-TG distance. The realignment surgery's geometric impact was measured. The poster quantifies it.
pmc-13531197: A 2026 cardiology paper on retrieval strategies for embolized left atrial appendage closure devices. The escaped devices needed recapture. The strategies are the guidance.
pmc-13501897: In this 2026 cardiology paper, the hs-CRP-to-albumin ratio correlated with all-cause mortality in acute exacerbation of chronic heart failure. The inflammatory-nutritional ratio predicted death. The correlation is the risk tool.
pmc-13500897: In this 2026 neuroimaging paper, social dysfunction in ADHD children was associated with increased amygdala functional connectivity instability — via static and dynamic connectivity analysis (the title is truncated). The unstable amygdala explained social struggles. The dynamic analysis is the advance.
pmc-13488397: This 2026 green chemistry paper reported mechanochemical sustainable synthesis of platinum(II) complexes — reactivity inversion and coordination mode control. The ball-mill chemistry was sustainable. The synthesis is the advance.
pmc-13470597: This 2026 case report described chronic pediatric ankle swelling due to an occult foreign body. The hidden splinter explained the years of swelling. The case is the reminder.
pmc-13442597: This 2026 Korean study associated weekend warrior and regular activity patterns with hypertension prevalence by socioeconomic status in adults. The activity pattern's benefit varied by class. The associations inform public health.
pmc-13432797: This 2026 paper showed isobavachin attenuated renal and cardiac injury in chronic hyperuricemia via NF-kB and NLRP3 pathway modulation. The plant compound protected kidney and heart. The modulation is the mechanism.
pmc-13464497: A 2026 plant physiology paper: "When does embolism become too much?" — crossing the point of no return and still surviving. The xylem's resilience was probed. The surviving is the paradox.
pmc-13639697: A 2026 prostate cancer paper on cardio-cerebrovascular diseases' impact on enzalutamide and abiraterone treatment in castration-resistant disease. The heart comorbidity's treatment impact was measured. The impact guides oncology.
pmc-13576097: A 2026 cross-sectional study of post-traumatic dental care, mouthguard use, and preventive behavior among athletes in sports of different contact intensities (the title is truncated). The athletes' dental habits were surveyed. The behaviors inform prevention.
pmc-13526797: This 2026 chemistry paper reported decarboxylative epoxidation of carboxylic acids for accelerating oxirane synthesis and derivatives. The reaction was sped up. The epoxidation expands synthesis.
pmc-13426097: A 2026 paper: magnetoelectric nanoparticles enabled modulation of cortical networks by low-intensity static magnetic fields in vitro. The nanoparticles steered brain networks. The enabling is the neurotechnology.
pmc-13472797: This 2026 exploratory model examined malnutrition's mediating role in associations between oral frailty, food insecurity, and depression among rural older adults (the title is truncated). The malnutrition pathway was modeled. The mediating role is the insight.
pmc-13599697: In this 2026 paper, visual responsivity in autism was measured in autistic and non-autistic adults using psychophysics, fMRI, and EEG. The autistic visual brain was probed. The measuring is the multi-modal insight.
pmc-13485097: A 2026 scoping review of the internet of things in assistive technology for people with visual impairment. The IoT aids were mapped. The review is the technology outlook.
pmc-13424797: A 2026 comparative outcomes study of open, laparoscopic, and robot-assisted radical cystectomy using IPTW-adjusted trifecta and pentafecta metrics. The bladder removal approaches were head-to-head. The outcomes inform urology.
pmc-13571397: In this 2026 case report, a first diagonal to left ventricle fistula with LAD collateral flow was described. The coronary anomaly was documented. The case is the rarity.
arxiv-2606-16297: The gamma-ray sky glows with mysterious light, and astronomers want to know what produces it. This paper cross-correlates gamma-ray maps with galaxy catalogs from DESI DR2 and unWISE — a "tomography" that slices the glow by distance. The technique reveals which cosmic structures the gamma rays come from.
